title: Fuel and Electrical Systems Technician (Sgt to LCpl) NMOS (1164, 1341, 2141, 2146, 2147, 3521), DC I&L
raw_text:
3. MOS 3524, Fuel and Electrical Systems Technician (Sgt to LCpl) NMOS
(1164, 1341, 2141, 2146, 2147, 3521), DC I&L

    a. Summary. The Fuel and Electrical Systems Technician provides field/
intermediate level maintenance of fuel, electrical, air induction, and
tactical vehicle personnel heater components. This MOS will be assigned as a
NMOS only.




                                         3-283                           Enclosure (1)
 3129                                                                NAVMC 1200.1L



    b. Prerequisites.        Must hold MOS 1164, 1341, 2141, 2146, 2147, or 3521
as a primary MOS.

    c. Requirements. Complete the Fuel and Electrical Systems Component
Repair Course (M03ACP7), Marine Corps Combat Service Support School, Camp
Lejeune, NC.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (x), Motor Transport Training and Readiness Manual.

            (5) Light Armored Vehicle (LAV) Repairer/Technician, 2147.

            (6) Automotive Maintenance Technician, 3521.

            (7) Crash/Fire/Rescue Vehicle Technician, 3526.

Qualifications required include operation and maintenance skills of automotive vehicles. The duties require highly technical skills supplemented by administrative and managerial skills. body:
The Motor Transport Occupational Field (OccFld) includes the licensing, operation, employment, maneuver, and maintenance functions for motor transport tactical wheeled vehicles and equipment in support of combat and garrison operations. Qualifications required include operation and maintenance skills of automotive vehicles. The duties require highly technical skills supplemented by administrative and managerial skills. Motor Transport Marines will be required to learn licensing procedures, vehicle operation and maintenance procedures, personnel and operational management techniques, preparation of orders and directives and record keeping procedures. Formal schooling and standardized training is provided to Marines entering this Occupational Field. Types of entry-level jobs available include work as Tactical Wheeled Vehicle Operator and Field/ Intermediate Maintenance Technician. There is a wide variety of billets available in the OccFld ranging from duty at all staff levels of MAGTF to the opportunity to serve in smaller organizations/units.

3. MOS 3524, Fuel and Electrical Systems Technician (Sgt to LCpl) NMOS (1164, 1341, 2141, 2146, 2147, 3521), DC I&L a. Summary. The Fuel and Electrical Systems Technician provides field/ intermediate level maintenance of fuel, electrical, air induction, and tactical vehicle personnel heater components. This MOS will be assigned as a NMOS only. b. Prerequisites. Must hold MOS 1164, 1341, 2141, 2146, 2147, or 3521 as a primary MOS. c. Requirements. Complete the Fuel and Electrical Systems Component Repair Course (M03ACP7), Marine Corps Combat Service Support School, Camp Lejeune, NC. d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (x), Motor Transport Training and Readiness Manual.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade.
